one_liner: Supabase has a free tier with a Management API (OAuth2 authorization-code flow), per-project REST and GraphQL APIs, and a vendor-namespaced MCP server in the MCP registry.
auth_notes: The pages show an OAuth authorization-code flow for the Management API. API keys (publishable and secret) and personal access tokens are not shown in the supplied pages. API_KEY is kept from the draft and Composio signals (Composio lists OAUTH2 and API_KEY) and is low confidence. Publishing an integration in the Dashboard needs partner approval, but building an OAuth client does not appear to.
access_notes: The Free plan costs $0 and includes unlimited API requests. It allows 2 active projects, and free projects pause after 1 week of inactivity. The pages do not show where OAuth apps or tokens are created, so the self-serve claim is inferred.
blocker_notes: There is no major blocker. Free projects pause after inactivity. Project-scoped and read-only access is listed under the Team plan. Listing an OAuth integration as a Dashboard partner requires a Supabase Program Authorization.

evidence.quote: Supabase shows a consent screen. Once the user consents, Supabase redirects back to the partner with an authorization code.
